title: PIT available_time semantics
content: event_time is when an economic or market event occurred. available_time is the earliest time the information could legitimately be known by the strategy or data consumer. processing_time is when the platform ingested, normalized, or processed the record. revision_id identifies a revision of the same logical observation. A backtest must not use a record before available_time, even when event_time is earlier and the record is present in a later snapshot. This separation prevents look-ahead bias. Example: an earnings release with event_time 2026-01-10 and available_time 2026-01-11 08:00 UTC must not affect a decision at 2026-01-10 close.

provenance.note: Initial domain artifact created from the platform requirements; not a claim of repository verification.

tests.name: revision-preserved
tests.assertion: revision_id is retained when observations are revised

Documented as market first-known time; modeled and persisted; get_pit filters available_time <= as_of_time; future unavailable record returns None.
Modeled and persisted; normalizer maps it from raw.ingest_time.
Implementation and tests support revision_id=2 and latest available version; README known limitation says revision_id currently defaults to/was planned as constant 1, creating documentation conflict.
Repository query gates rows by available_time <= as_of_time; test asserts unavailable future data returns None.
README example and tests cover an event_time later visible only after available_time.

gaps_found: PIT semantics are implemented only on the financial side: neither src/domain/price.py nor src/repositories/price.py carries available_time, so the artifact's applies_to entries 'backtesting' and 'factor-calculation' are not yet enforced outside financial_fact

revision_id exists as a column and in the UNIQUE key, but there is no revision-writing path: save() uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a corrected value at the same (symbol, metric_name, event_time, revision_id) is silently dropped instead of becoming a new revision
no ordering invariant is validated (ann_date >= end_date is never asserted in src/validators/financial.py), so available_time < event_time would pass silently
